# City of Malden

Malden City Hall · 215 Pleasant Street · Malden, MA 02148

# Meeting Minutes - Final · City Council

Council President Amanda Linehan · Councillor at Large Karen Colon Hayes · Councillor Paul Condon · Councillor Peg Crowe · Councillor at Large Michelle Luong · Councillor at Large Carey McDonald · Councillor Ryan O'Malley · Councillor Jadeane Sica · Councillor Chris Simonelli · Councillor Ari Taylor · Councillor Stephen Winslow

Tuesday, April 21, 2026 · 7:00 PM · City Council Chambers · 215 Pleasant Street · Malden, MA 02148 · Watch the meeting with Teams: https://tinyurl.com/39t2ram3

## 1. CALL TO ORDER

Council President Linehan called the meeting to order at 7:14 PM.

## 2. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE & MOMENT OF SILENCE IN HONOR OF SERVICE MEMBERS

An additional moment of silence was offered by Councillor Simonelli in honor of Wayne Martineau from the Inspectional Services Department who passed away on April 20 at the age of 66, after battling a long illness.

## 3. ROLL CALL

Councillor McDonald was in attendance via Teams so every vote this evening was done by roll call.

Also in attendance was Christopher Mooney, Maria Luise, Paul Myers, and Lisa Cagno.

Present - Councillors: 11 - Karen Colon Hayes, Paul Condon, Peg Crowe, Amanda Linehan, Carey McDonald, Ryan O'Malley, Jadeane Sica, Chris Simonelli, Ari Taylor, Stephen Winslow and Michelle Luong

## 4. GUESTS, CITIZEN ACHIEVEMENT, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

**229-26** 

Representatives from Malden Safe Streets and Safe Routes to School, accompanied by Malden's School Crossing Guards will appear before the Council to present on a new safety initiative being rolled out for the school population.

Attachments: Malden_Crossing Guards Council presentation 4.21.26

Tina Hein, Outreach Coordinator with Safe Routes to School, Allie Durak, President of Malden Safe Streets, and Gina Hayes, 2025 Massachusetts Crossing Guard of the Year appeared before the Council to present a new safety initiative to improve conditions for school crossing guards, focusing on snow removal, mapping, and community collaboration.

## 5. PUBLIC COMMENT

## 6. CONSENT AGENDA

### Approval of the Consent Agenda

A motion was made by Councillor Crowe, seconded by Councillor Condon, that this be approved on the Consent Agenda. The motion carried by the following vote:

Councillor Simonelli was not present in the Chambers at the time this vote was taken.

Yea: 10 - Colon Hayes, Condon, Crowe, Linehan, McDonald, O'Malley, Sica, Taylor, Winslow

and Luong

## 7. APPOINTMENTS & ELECTIONS

**224-26** 

Mayoral Reappointment: John P. King of 67 Upham Street, Malden, as member of the Board of Appeal, having served since 2000, said term to commence upon confirmation by the City Council and expire May 1, 2029.

Sponsors: Peg Crowe

Attachments: Mayor's Reappointment Letter - John King

A motion was made by Councillor Crowe, seconded by Councillor Sica, that the Appointment be confirmed. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 11 - Colon Hayes, Condon, Crowe, Linehan, McDonald, O'Malley, Sica, Simonelli, Taylor, Winslow and Luong

**225-26** 

Mayoral Reappointment: William Hurley of 67 Kimball Street, Malden as the labor member of the Malden Housing Authority Board, having served since 2020, said term to commence upon confirmation by the City Council and expire May 2, 2031.

Yea: 11 - Colon Hayes, Condon, Crowe, Linehan, McDonald, O'Malley, Sica, Simonelli, Taylor, Winslow and Luong

## 8. COMMUNICATIONS

**226-26** 

Communication: Community Preservation Committee appropriation orders for seven different projects and programs have been sent by the Mayor’s Office directly to the Finance Committee to avoid delays on the City Council’s review and approval thereof. All seven orders will come back before the Full Council with recommendations for a final vote after review by the Finance Committee

Sponsors: Amanda Linehan

A motion was made by Councillor Winslow, seconded by Councillor Simonelli, that the Communication be placed on file. The motion carried by the following vote:

headline: Confirmed two board reappointments and granted seventeen license petitions while referring six others to committee.
summary: The Council heard a presentation from Safe Routes to School and Malden Safe Streets on a new safety initiative for school crossing guards. It approved past meeting minutes, placed one appointment and one communication on file, confirmed two mayoral reappointments, referred six license petitions to the License Committee, and granted seventeen license and hours petitions recommended by the License Committee. Three National Grid utility petitions remained tabled with no vote recorded.
